## Description

A large, linear pennate diatom (50–170 × 10–30 µm) with a striated frustule and a clearly visible
raphe through which it secretes mucilage to glide on the glass: the classroom gliding diatom.
Frequent in ponds, peat bogs and wet moss.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 0.5), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 4 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Raphe gliding](../../mechanics/locomotion.md) with the speed of *Navicula* (no measured value). The real valve is
linear with parallel sides; here it is an elongated ellipse (squareness 2), because with a cylinder the
division furrow does not close.
